name: Myokoku-ji no Sotetsu (the Homesick Cycad)

location.address: Myokoku-ji Temple, 4-1-4 Zaimokucho-higashi, Sakai-ku, Sakai, Osaka Prefecture, Japan
location.neighbourhood: Sakai, roughly 20-25 minutes by Nankai train from central Osaka (Namba)

access: Paid entry to the temple grounds: adults 400 yen, elementary/junior-high students 200 yen. Open 10:00-16:30; groups of 15 or more need a reservation. The temple runs special spring and autumn public viewing periods for the cycad garden (2024's spring viewing ran 26-27 March with an evening illumination on the 26th); photography is reported prohibited inside the temple buildings, worth flagging for a visitor.
transport: Nearest station Sakai-Higashi or Sakai-shi (Nankai lines) or JR Sakai-shi, roughly 10-15 minutes' walk from the temple; about 20-25 minutes by train from Namba in central Osaka.
verify_notes: One of Japan's most famous individual trees, nicknamed 'Sotetsu no Tera' (Cycad Temple) after this one specimen; it is the reason people visit. Grouped locally as one of 'Japan's Three Great Cycads' alongside Ryoka-ji (Shizuoka) and Noman-ji (Yoshida, Shizuoka) -- note Noman-ji's cycad is already published on this site as yos_001 in yoshida.json, which corroborates this tree's standing rather than being a coincidence. DESIGNATION DATE CONFLICT, flagging rather than picking a winner: English Wikipedia gives 1923-12-13; the dedicated Japanese Wikipedia article '妙國寺のソテツ' gives 1924-12-09 and adds it was the first cycad ever given the designation. Age over 1,100 years is repeated by both Wikipedia language versions and the Sakai tourism board with no independent dating method cited -- treated as a traditional estimate and kept as a broad band rather than sharpened. The claim in one candidate photo's filename that this is 'Japan's oldest cycad' was checked against the dedicated Japanese Wikipedia article and is NOT made there or in any other source found; do not repeat that superlative in the story. CONDITION HISTORY: visible decline (yellowing leaf tips) was recorded by 1999, and a dedicated 'Myokoku-ji Cycad Revitalization Committee' ran a restoration programme 2008-2011; a 2008 survey of the healthiest sub-clump (29 trunks) recorded a base circumference of 387cm and a largest single trunk circumference of 250cm at 1.3m height. No condition report was found past 2012, but the 2024 spring viewing events (below) are more recent, indirect evidence the grove is still maintained as a going concern. LEGEND (the tree's main draw): warlord Oda Nobunaga had it transplanted to his Azuchi Castle around 1580; it allegedly cried every night to return to Sakai, and when Nobunaga ordered it cut down it bled and writhed like a serpent, frightening him into returning it to the temple, where a shrine (Ugatoku-ryujin) now marks the spot. Documented in the Edo-period gazetteer 'Izumi Meisho-zue'. PHYSICAL: this is a colony/clump of roughly 120 trunks and branches of varying sizes growing from one base rather than a single trunk (typical of very old Cycas revoluta), so a single girth figure is not meaningful -- left girth_cm empty rather than force a number; one source gives a stem diameter over 1.7m and height figures of 7-8m vary slightly between sources. CONDITION/ALIVE: temple actively runs the garden as its main attraction with dated 2024 spring viewing events (26-27 March, evening illumination), which is recent, direct evidence the tree and garden are open and maintained today, not merely a historical record. ACCESS: paid entry, ordinary temple visiting hours, no restriction beyond the fee -- clean pass under hard rule 10. DESTINATION TEST: passes clearly, arguably the strongest of this batch -- the temple is literally named for this tree in popular usage, it has its own Wikipedia article independent of a Japan-wide giant-tree list, and it draws dedicated spring/autumn viewing crowds. CONTAINER: do NOT treat as a standalone single-famous-tree place. Sakai borders Osaka city and Myokoku-ji sits about 20-25 minutes by train from central Osaka (Namba), well inside CLAUDE.md's 30-minute day-trip boundary, and Osaka is already published (data/cities/osaka.json, 5 trees, ids osa_001-005). Recommend adding this as osa_006 to the Osaka city file with the neighbourhood/address honestly naming Sakai, per the Blarney-counts-for-Cork precedent, rather than creating a new single-tree place.
